- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overpredicts in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply a 1–2% downward bias early in the forecast.
- If sentiment shows a clear reversal (e.g., from positive to negative or vice versa), model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- In periods of high volatility (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days with sentiment > 0.67 or < -0.33), model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing or reduce weight on recent data.
